title: Onprem VPC compatibility matrix and TF slim modules (draft)
content:
Purpose
This note collects an initial compatibility matrix for common customer on‑prem/cloud hybrid environments and proposes a set of small, composable Terraform modules ("slim modules") we can standardize for VPC bootstrap, edge connector, and SRV/ingress wiring. It's intentionally pragmatic: focus on minimal landings to reduce customer blast radius and speed onboarding.

Scope and audience
- Audience: solutions engineering, private-deployments SREs, customer onboarding engineers.
- Scope: customer VPC/network preflight, minimal TF module API, upgrade/rollback plan for customers migrating from legacy larger modules.
- Not in scope: PKI issuance policies (we link to PKI playbook), downstream application configuration (handled by tenant ops).

High-level recommendations
- Ship a 3-module reference: vpc-bootstrap, connector-edge, ingress-routes. Each module exposes a very small surface area (CIDR, egress policy, nat config, optional peering).
- Provide a compatibility matrix mapping typical customer constraints to recommended module flags.
- Default module behavior should be no-destructive: create new resources with unique suffixes rather than replacing customer names.
- Include a small "migration helper" script (bash + terraform plan parsing) to auto-detect conflicting state and offer rename/recreate suggestions.

Compatibility matrix (summary rows – expand in onboarding playbook)
Columns: customer environment constraint -> recommended mode / TF flag / notes
- Strict egress-only firewall (outbound whitelisting only) -> connector-edge.allow_outbound_only = true; preflight: list of outbound ports required (443, 80, 5228 for metrics). Recommend using TLS proxy if deep inspection present.
- Fixed MTU <= 1500 (legacy MPLS) -> vpc-bootstrap.mtu = 1500; set path mtu discovery and ensure jumbo frames disabled on ephemeral bridges.
- Customer NAT with overlapping private CIDRs -> vpc-bootstrap.enable-pod-overlay = true; connector-edge.use-vpn-peers = true; recommend NAT64 translation if IPv6 required.
- No BGP support (static routing only) -> connector-edge.static-routes = [{dst, next_hop}]; document sample static route templates.
- On-prem firewalls performing TLS interception -> ingress-routes.force-cert-pinning = true; recommend mutual TLS to detect interception.
- HSM/KMS behind private network -> modules support kms_endpoint and a TLS trust_anchor field; do not attempt to auto-provision cloud KMS.
- Air-gapped (no internet) -> special build: modules.armory = true (disables fetchers, requires pre-seeded model artifacts). Provide separate onprem-airgap playbook.

Terraform slim modules design notes
1) vpc-bootstrap (purpose: minimal VPC + subnets + route table scaffolding)
- Inputs: name_prefix, cidr_block, public_subnet_cidrs, private_subnet_cidrs, mtu, nat_mode (none|managed|customer), dns_zone_optional
- Outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, route_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids (if managed)
- Behavior: non-invasive defaults, no destructive renames, tag resources with onboarding_id.
- Versioning: semantic v0.x until BC stable. Avoid provider version pinning in example, but recommend pinned providers in customer repos.

2) connector-edge (purpose: VPN/peer + edge instances + health proxies)
- Inputs: vpc_id, peer_type (vpn|direct|none), peer_config, allowed_outbound_ports, mtu, metrics_endpoint
- Flags: allow_outbound_only, use_vpn_peers, static_routes, edge_instance_count (min 1), health_check_port
- Notes: make the VPN config a list to support multi-cloud fallbacks. Provide a lightweight docker-based health proxy image as an example.

3) ingress-routes (purpose: secure route table entries/ingress proxies and DNS wiring)
- Inputs: internal_lb_arn_optional, external_lb_arn_optional, dns_zone, cert_arn_optional, routes (list of {prefix, target})
- Behavior: prefer non-global changes; if replacing LB, create new LB with onboarding suffix and then flip DNS. Provide an automated wait-and-check subflow.

Migration and upgrade plan (customer-facing checklist)
Preflight (run by SE/SRE)
- Confirm ownership and org-level approvals (ticket created, stakeholders listed).
- Run compatibility-check script: collects MTU, CIDR overlap, firewall outbound rules, BGP support, KMS endpoints. Script output: JSON summary.
- Capture current terraform state (s3/backends): snapshot -> store in secure location.
- Run terraform plan against modules in a staging account with planfile.

Canary rollout
- Deploy modules to 1 non-critical region/availability zone or tenant environment.
- Validate connectivity: ping, TLS handshake to metrics endpoint, example gen request to hosted-control-plane (if allowed).
- Run traffic shaping to send 5% of production traffic through new connector for 48 hours.

Full cutover
- Schedule a maintenance window only if forced (preferred path: rolling without downtime).
- Create new resources first (do not delete old ones until DNS and health checks pass for 30m).
- Swap DNS records with TTL 60s. Monitor for 60 minutes.

Rollback plan
- If health checks fail after DNS flip: revert DNS to previous records, mark modules for deletion in next maintenance window.
- If terraform drift blocks rollback: use state snapshot to rehydrate previous state and run 'terraform apply' with force-recreate where necessary. Document exact commands in playbook.

Testing matrix (automated)
- Integration tests: terraform plan > apply > basic connectivity probes > teardown. Keep tests in GH action matrix with small resource footprint.
- Edge cases: CIDR overlap scenarios; BGP-free environment; static-only routing test. Each should have an automated preflight assertion.

Operational observability
- Built-in metrics in connector-edge: connection_up, round_trip_ms, bytes_in/out, tls_handshake_success. Push to customer metrics endpoint or Prometheus remote write.
- Logging: edge instances log to central aggregator; include request_id header for traceability.
- Alerting: SLA breach -> automated fallback to managed-hosted connector.

Developer notes and TF implementation TODOs (quick list)
- Reduce module input list to essential 6 parameters.
- Implement "safe-create" helper: if resource tag with onboarding_id exists, do not re-create identical resources.
- Add a tiny migration helper that prints plan diffs as human-friendly steps (rename vs recreate).
- Write GH action that runs basic compatibility-check script as PR gating.

Open questions / unresolved items
- Should we maintain a separate airgapped module set or add an "airgap" switch? (Tradeoffs: complexity vs clarity).
- How far do we go in auto-detecting customer NAT + overlapping CIDR? For now, prefer explicit operator opt-in.
- Policy for KMS/HSM integration: require manual ticket to security for direct HSM binding.

Appendix: sample preflight command outputs (example)
- compatibility-check --target 10.11.0.0/16 --probe-hosts "control-plane.redwood.local" --out report.json
  sample report.json keys: mtu, cidr_overlap: false, outbound_allowed_ports: [443, 80], bgp: false, kms_reachable: true

References
- See linked Confluence index for full onboarding runbooks.
- Related GH PR: terraform-modules/pull/728 (early slim module sketch).

Notes to self
- Next: pair with Solutions Eng to run two customer pilots (one MPLS legacy customer, one direct cloud peering). Capture telemetry.
- Make sure this draft is reviewed before Q1 playbook freeze.
